subject: Life Skills
title: The Latte Factor Myth
description: A quick, practical guide to The Latte Factor Myth.

hook.text: Financial gurus say skip the $5 latte and you will be rich. The math works.

buildup.text: David Bach popularized the idea: $5 a day invested for 30 years becomes over $200,000. On paper, it is compelling.

discovery.text: The real problem is rarely lattes. It is rent, healthcare, student loans, and stagnant wages.

twist.text: Cutting all joy to save $5 causes budgeting burnout. People rebel against extreme austerity and spend even more later.

climax.text: Focus on the big three: housing, transportation, and food. Saving 10% on big costs beats eliminating every small.

punchline.text: Keep the latte. Cut the car payment instead.

quiz.question: Why does the 'latte factor' advice often fail?
options: Lattes are actually a good investment
Cutting small joys causes burnout while big costs are the real problem
Most people do not drink lattes
